finding.claim: LinkSanitizer is fail-open: TargetScrubber keeps every non-<a> element and every attribute except href, so script tags and on* event-handler attributes pass through. This is a low-severity, design-level candidate, not a confirmed exploitable bug; it matters only if callers treat LinkSanitizer output as safe HTML.
finding.source: Untrusted HTML string passed to sanitize(html) (lib/rails/html/sanitizer.rb:39-44), reaching LinkSanitizer (lib/rails/html/sanitizer.rb:244-249 for HTML4, 354-359 for HTML5).
finding.sink: Serialized output of LinkSanitizer (lib/rails/html/sanitizer.rb:32-34 and 190-192), which keeps <script> elements and on* attributes.

trace.note: Link#scrub runs the TargetScrubber over the fragment
PermitScrubber#scrub only removes a node when keep_node? is false
keep_node? calls allowed_node? when @tags is set
TargetScrubber#allowed_node? returns !super, so any element not named 'a' is kept (e.g. script)
scrub_attributes runs on the kept element
TargetScrubber#scrub_attribute? returns !super, so onclick is not marked for removal
scrub_attribute applies only URI-scheme, SVG-ref, and empty-src checks; it never removes on* attributes

finding.guards_checked: Enforced: the a-only gate and the href removal (scrubbers.rb:196-202). Not enforced: removal of script elements or on* attributes. The library does not claim LinkSanitizer sanitizes; its doc (sanitizer.rb:236-242) describes only stripping link tags. Installed Loofah 2.15.0 lacks scrub_uri_attribute, so URI-scheme checks for href are unverified.
